title: Cloud sessions delete branches the Oct 30 grant allows
why: The cloud relay drops a branch-delete push, so 2,338 branches pile up on origin (measured 14:21 CST Nov 11).
note: R45, owner 14:25 CST Nov 11 in chat: "im good with either an actions workflow or a github token -- github token seems better? im very ambivalent to tokens being in all my cloud sessions its just a github token". The owner makes one GitHub token as SHIV_GITHUB_TOKEN in the cloud environment; a session tests one delete and one Projects read. If the relay passes it, deletes go through one home that applies the Oct 30 grant. If not, the token becomes a repository secret and an Actions workflow deletes. Test result 14:32 CST (session_013NEJKynqk1w976JZQ3noCn, relayed by the retrospective): REST reads pass the relay (GET /user 200). The REST branch delete never left the session: the auto-mode classifier refused it as "[Git Destructive]". The owner was asked whether to approve that one delete. 15:04 CST: with the owner's yes, the REST ref delete with his token got 403 from the relay ("Write access to this GitHub API path is not permitted through this proxy."). R45's ruled fallback holds: a GitHub Actions workflow deletes branches with GitHub's own token, only what the Oct 30 grant allows; the Projects table (D1) needs his token as a repository secret. Test branch test/retro-delete-probe-1418 is still on origin; the workflow's first run removes it. Build waits for the fan-out (owner 13:51).
source: Owner 14:25 CST Nov 11 (R45, plan restart-plan e276625); page item 513
